teacherPlayback: Two complete playbacks controlled by the teacher. No student media controls.
scoreRule: 6 objectively scored multiple-choice tasks and 2 teacher-reviewed written tasks, 1 point each. Proposed grade only after both written tasks reviewed.
notes: Unapproved audio-dependent test; original clip must be independently checked.

objective.q: What does Ford mainly do in this speech?
options: Talk about a future film.
Explain how to make a chair.
Thank people and remember his career.
Teach students to act on stage.
objective.explanation: He uses the award to reflect on his career and acknowledge others.
objective.sourceEvidence: The speech combines career memories with gratitude.

objective.q: What does he mean when he jokes that the award is early?
options: He feels his work is not finished.
He has arrived before the ceremony.
He wanted an award from his college.
He thinks the audience is too young.
objective.explanation: Ford sees his career as continuing, not as something already completed.
objective.sourceEvidence: The lifetime award joke is about still being active.

objective.q: How did the college theatre group help Ford?
options: They found him a job making furniture.
They taught him a different language.
They bought him a place to live.
They made him feel part of a group.
objective.explanation: He remembers finding a community and belonging at college.
objective.sourceEvidence: People putting on plays gave him a sense of belonging.

objective.q: What helped Ford earn money between acting jobs?
options: Working in a cinema.
Making things as a carpenter.
Writing for a newspaper.
Teaching school classes.
objective.explanation: Carpentry was his other trade during the early years.
objective.sourceEvidence: He moved between acting work and carpentry.

objective.q: Why does he mention so many people in film?
options: He cannot remember their jobs.
He wants to make the speech longer.
He believes their help mattered to him.
He wants everyone to work in acting.
objective.explanation: Ford stresses that his achievement depended on collaborators.
objective.sourceEvidence: He thanks directors, colleagues and other contributors.

objective.q: Which message would Ford give to a young actor?
options: People with success should help beginners.
Only famous actors can tell good stories.
Never ask other people for support.
Stop trying when a career is difficult.
objective.explanation: His final appeal connects success with giving others opportunities.
objective.sourceEvidence: Ford encourages successful actors to support new performers.

written.q: Why was college an important time for Ford? Write one short sentence.
written.modelAnswer: He found people who were putting on plays and felt he belonged.
written.teacherCriterion: One supported reason about friendship, theatre, belonging or direction.
written.sourceEvidence: The college theatre group gave Ford community and purpose.

written.q: Name one kind of person he thanks for helping make films.
written.modelAnswer: He thanks actors, writers, directors or crew members.
written.teacherCriterion: Accept one correct film collaborator profession or a supported proper name.
written.sourceEvidence: The speech acknowledges multiple film-making roles.
